import Mathlib

namespace Test

universe u
variable {γ : Type u}

def Action : Type u :=
  sorry

def TambaraType : Type u :=
  sorry

class Tambara (action : Action) (P : γ → γ → Type u) : Type u where
  x : TambaraType

class TambaraList (actions : List Action) (P : γ → γ → Type u) : Type u where
  xs : List TambaraType

instance {P : γ → γ → Type u} : TambaraList [] P where
  xs := []

instance {P : γ → γ → Type u} {action actions}
[h₁ : Tambara action P] [h₂ : TambaraList actions P] :
TambaraList (action :: actions) P where
  xs := h₁.x :: h₂.xs

def TambaraOptic (actions : List Action) (α β ς τ : γ) : Type (u + 1) :=
  (P : γ → γ → Type u) → [TambaraList actions P] → P α β → P ς τ

def TambaraOptic.compose {actions₁ actions₂ : List Action}
{δ ω ς τ α β : γ} (x : TambaraOptic actions₁ δ ω ς τ) (y : TambaraOptic actions₂ α β δ τ) :
(P : _) → [TambaraList (actions₁ ++ actions₂) P] → P α β → P ς τ :=
  sorry

example {actions₁ actions₂ : List Action} {ς τ α β : γ} :
((P : _) → [TambaraList (actions₁ ++ actions₂) P] → P α β → P ς τ) =
TambaraOptic (actions₁ ++ actions₂) α β ς τ := rfl

class Profunctor (p : Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) where

  (p : Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _)

A Finset can be used instead of a List to avoid depending on the order. The issue is that for instances to be computable, TambActionSpec must have a computable decidability instance. However, type equality in general cannot be computable. One solution would be to add labels for certain types and keep labels as a separate structure, then implement corresponding instances for connecting labels to types. Not sure how practical that approach would be though.

Here is a small example of how to use Finset to store and retrieve instances in a computable way. Here we use ℕ instead of TambActionSpec, so we don't need separate labels.

Code

import Mathlib

class C (_ : ℕ) : Type where
  n : ℕ

class CS (s : Finset ℕ) : Type where
  get : (t : ℕ) → t ∈ s → ℕ

instance {t} : C t where
  n := t

instance : CS ∅ where
  get _ := nofun

instance {t} : CS {t} where
  get _ _ := t

instance {t ts} [h₁ : C t] [h₂ : CS ts] : CS (insert t ts) :=
  if h : t ∈ ts then by simpa [h] else .mk $ fun t₁ h₃ =>
  if h₄ : t₁ = t then h₁.n else h₂.get t₁ (by grind)

def f (ts : Finset ℕ) [h : CS ts] : ℕ :=
  ts.attach.fold (· + ·) 0 (fun ⟨t, h⟩ => CS.get t h)

example : f {1, 2, 3, 4} = 10 := rfl

import Mathlib
import Std

open Std

class Profunctor (p : Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) where
  map : (ς -> α) -> (β -> τ) -> p α β -> p ς τ

class Interp  (label : String × String)  (actionₗ actionᵣ : outParam (Type u -> Type v -> Type w)) where

class Tamb (label : String × String) [inst : Interp label ax ax'] (p : Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) [Profunctor p]
  where
  tambara : p α β  -> p (ax μ α) (ax' μ β)

class Interps (l : Finset (String × String)) (x : outParam (Std.HashMap (String × String) ((Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) × (Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _)))) where

instance [Interp label ax ax'] : Interps {label} {(label, (ax, ax'))} where

class Tambs (s : Finset (String × String)) [inst : Interps s axs] (p : Type _ -> Type _ -> Type _) [Profunctor p] where
  tambara {α β μ : Type u} : (label : (String × String)) -> (h : label ∈ axs) -> p α β -> p ((axs.get _ h).1 μ α) ((axs.get _ h).2 μ β)

instance [Interp label ax ax'] [Profunctor p] [Tamb label p] : Tambs {label} p where
  tambara := fun label' x =>
    have : label' = label := by simp at x; symm; assumption
    by subst this; simp; exact Tamb.tambara label'

instance : Profunctor (· -> ·) where
  map := fun f g h => (g ∘ h) ∘ f

instance : Interp ("Prod", "Prod") Prod Prod  where

instance {α : Type u} : Profunctor (fun x _ => x -> α) where
  map := fun f _ h => h ∘ f

instance : Tamb ("Prod", "Prod") (fun x _ => x -> α) where
  tambara := fun f x => f x.2

def ProfOptic (specs : Finset (String × String)) [Interps specs axs] (α β ς τ : Type _) :=
  {p : _} -> [Profunctor p] -> [Tambs specs p] -> p α β -> p ς τ

def Lens (α β ς τ) := ProfOptic {⟨"Prod", "Prod"⟩} α β ς τ
def Lens.mk
  (get : ς -> α)
  (set : ς -> β -> τ)
  : Lens α β ς τ
  := fun {_} prof tamb =>
  have := prof.map (fun s => (s, get s)) (Function.uncurry set)
  have thisa := tamb.tambara ("Prod", "Prod") (by simp) (μ := ς) (α := α) (β := β)
  this ∘ (by simp at thisa; exact thisa)

def mylens : Lens Nat Nat (Nat × Nat) (Nat × Nat) :=
  Lens.mk Prod.fst (fun (_, snd) new => (new, snd))

def view
  [Interps l axs]
  (x : ProfOptic l α β ς τ)
  [Tambs l (fun x _ => x -> α)]
  : ς -> α :=
    have := @x (fun x _ => x -> α)
    this id

In order to reason about a Haskell-like type system, where types with distinct names are indeed distinct, it is necessary to define the type system inductively, rather than relying on Lean types. In Lean, for instance, ℕ and ℕ × ℕ cannot be proved to be distinct. The conversion to Lean types should happen only at the end, and all reasoning must be done with the inductively defined type system. Something like this may be a promising approach:

Code

import Mathlib

def T : ℕ → Type 1
| 0 => Type
| n + 1 => Type → T n

class Info (name : String) : Type 1 where
  arity : ℕ
  toLean : T arity

inductive HType : ℕ → Type 1 where
| ref : (name : String) → [i : Info name] → HType i.arity
| app : {n : ℕ} → HType (n + 1) → HType 0 → HType n

instance : Info "Integer" where
  arity := 0
  toLean := ℤ

instance : Info "Prod" where
  arity := 2
  toLean := Prod

instance : Info "->" where
  arity := 2
  toLean := (· → ·)

def HType.toLean {n} : HType n → T n
| @HType.ref name h => h.toLean
| @HType.app _ t₁ t₂ => t₁.toLean t₂.toLean

def mkFuncType (x y : HType 0) : HType 0 :=
  .app (.app (.ref "->") x) y

def mkProdType (x y : HType 0) : HType 0 :=
  .app (.app (.ref "Prod") x) y

it seems the following will automate a proof of membership purely at the typeclass level (tyvm vlad for suggesting this is possible at all)

class IsElm (l : List α) (a : α) where
  i : Fin l.length
  wf : List.get _ i = a := by grind

instance : IsElm [a] a where
  i := 0

instance [inst : IsElm l a] : IsElm (a' :: l) a where
  i := inst.i.succ
  wf := have := inst.wf; by simp_all

class IsEq (a a' : α) where
  eq : a = a'

class IsNotEq (a a' : α) where
  noteq : a ≠ a'

class IsListHead (l : List α) (a : α) where
  wf : l.head? = .some a

instance : IsListHead [a] a where
  wf := by grind

instance : IsEq a a where
  eq := rfl

instance [IsEq a' a] [IsListHead (a' :: xs) a] : IsListHead (a' :: a'' :: xs) a where
  wf := by simp; exact IsEq.eq

instance [inst : IsListHead l a] : IsElm l a where
  i := ⟨0, by have := inst.wf; grind⟩
  wf := have := inst.wf; by simp; have := List.head?_eq_getElem? (l := l); grind

class IsInListBody (l : List α) (a : α)  where
  [iselm : IsElm l a]
  wf : ¬ l.head? = Option.some a

instance [IsNotEq a a']  : IsInListBody (a :: a' :: xs) a' where
  iselm := 1<:
  wf := by simp; exact IsNotEq.noteq

instance [inst : IsInListBody l a] : IsElm l a := inst.iselm

instance [inst : IsNotEq a a'] : IsNotEq a' a where
  noteq := have := inst.noteq; by grind

instance [IsInListBody l a] [IsNotEq a a'] : IsInListBody (a' :: l) a where
  wf := by simp; exact IsNotEq.noteq

abbrev myuniv : Univ := [("blah", Int), ("Bool", Bool), ("Nat", Nat), ("Int", Int)]

/-- info: instIsElmCons -/
#guard_msgs in
#synth IsElm myuniv ("Int", Int)
